decisions.rationale: The span names a single, specific disease: G6PD deficiency of the Mediterranean type. It is one defined condition, not a family of diseases, and the span includes the full qualifier needed for the most specific form.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease); What to Annotate 5 (minimum necessary span)

decisions.rationale: Favism is a single, specific hemolytic disease triggered by fava bean ingestion in G6PD-deficient individuals, with one definition and no further categorization.
Hemolytic anemia is a broad category that covers multiple distinct specific diseases with different causes, so it is a family of diseases rather than one specific disease.
G6PD Mediterranean is a named, specific variant form of G6PD deficiency with a single definition, so it is annotated as a Specific Disease.
G6PD Athens-like is a named, specific variant form of G6PD deficiency with one definition and no further categorization.
G6PD Union is a named, specific variant form of G6PD deficiency with one definition and no further categorization.
G6PD Betica is a named, specific deficient variant described in the text as a single form of G6PD deficiency, so it is a Specific Disease.
G6PD Menorca is a named, specific deficient variant of G6PD with a single definition, so it is a Specific Disease.

Here 'G6PD' is the abbreviation of the enzyme glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase, which refers to a gene or protein rather than to a disease. The bare abbreviation does not name a disease and is not annotated.
